newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius rupee firms on dollar and pound.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius rupee firms on dollar and pound.

text.p: The Mauritian rupee firmed against both the dollar and pound on Wednesday, reflecting international trends, forex dealers said.
The rupee traded at a mean commercial rate of 20.0985 against the dollar from 20.1635 on Tuesday. On the pound, the rupee was quoted at a mean of 32.0205 from 32.0305 on Tuesday.
Dealers said the stronger rupee only reflected a weaker dollar in overnight international markets but was showing signs of weakness against other major currencies.
"The rupee is depreciating slightly on a weighted basis, that is when you also look at it against the German mark and the French franc," one dealer said.
The dealer said the weakening rupee versus these currencies resulted from importers' forex demand exceeding hard currency inflows from the island's main export sectors.
"With this situation prevailing, commercial banks are running short in their foreign exchange reserves. They were (short) before the central bank intervened on Monday," the dealer said.
During Monday's intervention, the central bank sold dollars to commercial banks at the prevailing interbank ask rate.
